To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a theoretical framework was developed to (1) simulate and assess the fundamental performance (in terms of HMI displacement ratios and lesion size) of HMIFU, and (2) demonstrate the feasibility of HMIFIU for HIFUS lesion detection based on tissue elasticity changes, through experimental validations.
a customized finite-element-based framework of harmonic motion imaging for HIFU was developed to assess the performance of HMIFUs for HIFU therapy monitoring.
a theoretical framework for HMIFU is established and the fundamental performance of this HIFU monitoring method is assessed and validated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a 3-D FE-based theoretical framework for HMIFU and its experimental validation.
the theoretical framework of HMIPU for HIFUS therapy monitoring and provides a basis for the future clinical applications of HMIPU
the theoretical and experimental study of the HMIFI system for HIFU monitoring and provides a theoretical foundation for the future development of HMIFU.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this study provides a solid foundation for future HMIFU studies, such as the optimization of the system design, the development of the HMIFUMI reconstruction algorithm, the investigation of the HIFU treatment planning and the clinical application of HMIFU.
the developed framework is capable of assessing the performance of HMIFUs in detecting HIFUs lesions.

the developed framework has demonstrated that HMIFU can detect HIFU lesions by measuring the increase of tissue apparent elasticity, and the HMI displacement ratio and lesion size growth are both proportional to the lesion-to-background Youngs modulus ratio and exposure time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the developed framework is a promising tool in assessing the HMIFU performance in HIFU lesion imaging, and it could be further applied in the design of the HMIFUS system for clinical use.

the developed theoretical framework can be used to guide the design and optimization of HIFU treatment planning, and the HMIFU method can be used as a real-time monitoring technique to assess the HIFU therapy outcome in a clinical setting.
a theoretical framework was developed for HMIFU lesion detection and quantification.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HMIFU can be used as a noninvasive monitoring tool for the HIFU treatment outcome.
HMIFU is feasible for lesion detection, and it is a promising tool for HIFU monitoring.
the developed HMIFU framework is a useful tool for HMIFU system design, performance assessment and optimization, and can be used to guide future in vivo HMIFU studies.
